units.title: Proofreading practice
units.summary: Leave 5 minutes to proofread. Read slowly, checking sentence endings, agreement, apostrophes and homophones, and correct errors neatly.

questions.prompt: What is wrong with “there childhood” (line 1)?
options: It should be ‘their’, meaning belonging to them.
It should be ‘they’re’.
‘childhood’ is spelt wrongly.
Nothing is wrong.
questions.explanation: The childhood belongs to the people, so the possessive ‘their’ is needed.

questions.prompt: “to expensive” (line 4) should be:
options: ‘too expensive’
‘two expensive’
‘to expencive’
It is correct.
questions.explanation: ‘too’ means ‘more than enough’. ‘to’ is a preposition or part of a verb (to swim).

questions.prompt: “The changing rooms was falling apart” (line 5). What is the error?
options: The verb should agree with the plural subject: ‘were’.
‘changing’ needs a capital letter.
‘apart’ should be ‘a part’.
There is no error.
questions.explanation: ‘rooms’ is plural, so the verb must be ‘were’. The November 2024 Paper 2 examiner report listed agreement errors among common weaknesses.
questions.misconception: Using a singular verb with a plural subject.

questions.prompt: Choose all the errors in lines 10 to 12.
options: “the pools empty”
“Weeds is growing”
“It effects everyone”
“fenced off”
“what we have lost”
questions.explanation: It should be ‘the pool’s empty’ (the pool is), ‘Weeds are growing’ and ‘It affects everyone’.

questions.prompt:
Which correction of lines 7 to 9 is better?
Version A: ‘But the pool was more than a place to swim, it was where you went …’ (unchanged)
Version B: ‘But the pool was more than a place to swim. It was where you went …’
options: Version A
Version B, because it replaces the comma splice with a full stop
Both are equally correct
Neither is correct
questions.explanation: The original joins 2 main clauses with a comma. A full stop (or a semicolon) corrects it.

questions.prompt: Why do so many people write ‘should of’ instead of ‘should have’?
options: Spoken ‘should’ve’ sounds like ‘should of’.
‘should of’ is the older correct form.
It is the American spelling.
‘of’ is a verb.
questions.explanation: ‘should’ve’ is short for ‘should have’. ‘Of’ is never correct after should, could or would.
questions.misconception: Writing ‘should of’ for ‘should have’.

questions.prompt: Match each error to its correction.
questions.explanation: Each of these is a common slip that a careful final read can catch.

questions.prompt: While proofreading, a student changes “Other towns have found ways to save their pools.” (line 13) to ‘there pools’. Is this right?
options: No: ‘their’ (belonging to them) was already correct.
Yes: ‘there’ is always right before a noun.
Yes: ‘their’ is an informal spelling.
It makes no difference.
questions.explanation: Proofreading can introduce errors as well as remove them. Check the meaning before you change a word.

questions.prompt: Rewrite lines 4 to 9 with all the errors corrected.
questions.model: Model answer: The council said it was too expensive to repair. There may be some truth in that. The changing rooms were falling apart and the water was always freezing, even in August. But the pool was more than a place to swim. It was where you went on the first hot day of the year and where you learned to be brave on the high board.
checklist: Corrects ‘to’ to ‘too’
Corrects ‘Their’ to ‘There’
Corrects ‘was’ to ‘were’
Fixes the comma splice in lines 7 to 8
Introduces no new errors
questions.explanation: There are 4 errors in these lines. A slow, line-by-line read finds more than a quick skim.

questions.prompt: The draft contains 10 deliberate errors. List each error and its correction.
questions.model: Model answer: 1. there → their (line 1). 2. to → too (line 4). 3. Their → There (line 4). 4. was → were (line 5). 5. comma splice after ‘swim’ → full stop and ‘It’ (line 7). 6. pools → pool’s (line 10). 7. is → are (line 10). 8. effects → affects (line 11). 9. should of → should have (line 16). 10. Its → It’s (line 16).
checklist: Finds the homophone errors (there, to, Their, effects)
Finds the agreement errors (was, is)
Finds the apostrophe errors (pools, Its)
Finds the comma splice and ‘should of’
Gives a correct version of each
questions.explanation: Grouping errors by type (homophones, agreement, apostrophes, demarcation) is a quick way to check you have found them all.
